# Sufficient repeated-axis normalization rule

Let C_v=((1+i)I+(1-i)X_v)/2 for a binary translation X_v. Direct expansion gives
C_v^2=X_v and C_v^4=I; translations and all C_v commute. Suppose a physical
owner remains idle between its actual previous touch and next touch. Each
complete normalized helper invocation has one distinct whole owner and leaves
exactly its declared C factors on that owner's assigned axes while restoring
borrowed spectators and all private workspace, for arbitrary initial dirt.

Axis v may occur k_v times across different completed invocations in that idle
window. Choose e_v in {0,1} so k_v+e_v is odd. Emit a residual child on all axes
with e_v=1 and an explicit translation X_v to the power (1-k_v-e_v)/2. Then
C_v^(k_v+e_v) X_v^((1-k_v-e_v)/2)=C_v exactly. Apply this independently to every
axis of the original pending child. The result is its original endpoint; no
physical owner is split, and no invocation is interleaved internally.

All actual axes, charts, multiplicities, parity-complement remainder and final
translations must be serialized and charged. Scalar and prefix invoices must
include the added translations. A repeated even pair loses two units of covered
rank relative to disjoint placement, so the original fixed deficit cannot be
assumed. The existing audit's disjointness rule must be replaced by this exact
ledger only for a new explicitly versioned program.

This is a sufficient new construction rule, independently reviewed by the
complex lane under the same normalized-invocation contract. A bounded full-stock
screen chose no overlaps, so this note claims no achieved kappa gain. It is not
permission to treat repeated calls or translations as free.
